evidence.text:
[K-MHW#1] Defining marine heatwaves: Hobday et al. (2016) define a marine heatwave as a discrete, prolonged, anomalously warm water event: sea surface temperature above the seasonally varying 90th percentile of a baseline climatology (ideally 30 years) for at least five consecutive days. Gaps of two days or less between events are treated as one event.

[K-SOURCES#4] Real marine data sources for replacing the ORCA demo data: ICAR-CMFRI publishes annual marine fish landing estimates by state and resource. The Centre for Marine Living Resources and Ecology (CMLRE) runs fishery and biodiversity surveys in the Indian EEZ and contributes records to IndOBIS.

[K-SOURCES#3] Real marine data sources for replacing the ORCA demo data: NOAA OISST (daily optimum interpolation SST) and NOAA Coral Reef Watch provide sea surface temperature and Degree Heating Weeks. Copernicus Marine Service distributes chlorophyll, salinity and oxygen products. INCOIS (Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services) provides regional ocean observations and forecasts.
